title: Benchmarking Agentic Systems in Automated Scientific Information Extraction with ChemX
experiments_summary: The study evaluated automated chemical information extraction using two datasets from the ChemX benchmark: nanozymes (nanomaterials domain) and chelate complexes (small molecules domain), both classified as lowest complexity. Two open-access articles per dataset were selected for reproducibility. The extraction task was defined as end-to-end: given an article file or DOI, systems must output structured extracted information according to a provided prompt. Evaluated systems included: (1) baseline LLMs GPT-5 and GPT-5 Thinking; (2) a general-purpose ChatGPT Agent; (3) domain-specific agentic systems including FutureHouse, SLM-Matrix, Eunomia Agent, ChemOpenIE, and nanoMINER. A custom single-agent preprocessing pipeline was also developed using the marker-pdf SDK to extract text blocks, tables, and images, converting them to markdown with GPT-4o-generated image descriptions inserted via tags, followed by extraction using GPT-4.1, GPT-5, and GPT-OSS-20b. Prompts were standardized templates requiring JSON array output with domain-specific fields (e.g., formula, km_value, SMILES, target_value). Extraction quality was measured using precision, recall, and F1 score computed per PDF via true positives, false positives, and false negatives, then averaged across PDFs. Systems unable to produce valid output structures or performing only partial extraction (e.g., Open-ChemIE, Eunomia) were excluded from quantitative comparison. A qualitative assessment was also conducted evaluating systems on PDF processing capability, output structure compliance, multimodality support, domain generalizability, and completeness of extraction.
